slides.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
slides.highlight: This work uses a VLA model with temporal tactile encoding and compliance control to infer human taking intent during handovers, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A multimodal humanoid handover system combining temporal tactile encoding and compliance for reliable, intent-aware object release.
card.key_idea: Finetuned GR00T VLA model using RGB, proprioception, and a frozen autoencoder that compresses ~0.9s of tactile history, paired with a low-level compliance controller to reduce interaction forces.
card.evaluation: Human-subject study (10 participants, 300 trials) comparing full system against no-tactile and no-compliance baselines using success rates, release delay, and subjective Likert scales.
card.limitation: Occasional failures occur during impulsive pulls that mimic genuine taking intent, and performance varies slightly based on individual user preferences for smoothness.

slides.title: Dressing in Motion: A Human Motion-Aware Diffusion Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing
slides.tldr: MOTION-AWARE DIFFUSION POLICY FOR ROBOTIC DRESSING
slides.highlight: This research introduces a visuomotor policy that enables robots to assist with dressing by adapting to dynamic human arm movements using point clouds and PDE diffusion.

card.one_liner: A robot-assisted dressing policy that adapts to dynamic human arm movements using diffusion and point-cloud registration.
card.key_idea: Combines a visuomotor diffusion policy learned from static demonstrations with a PDE-diffused scalar field and GICP registration to adapt trajectories to real-time arm motion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and a real-world study (9 participants, 3 garments, 6 motion patterns); outperformed 6 baselines in dressing ratio and user comfort.
card.limitation: Performance degrades during high-intensity arm swings (80-100cm amplitude, 0.8-1.0Hz frequency) and may struggle with alignment if motion occurs before insertion.

slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich assistive tasks using a deformable human model and physics-aware scoring. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction in care settings.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion does not imply physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated against manikin force-indentation measurements with a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol and physics-aware scoring (force, joint-limits, stability).
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs each). Results show task success often hides physical safety failures.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue; upper-arm calibration is reused from forearm; limited to a single robotic-bathing scenario.

slides.title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research introduces FWBC-VLA, which integrates a sensorless residual-torque estimator with a VLA model to enable wheeled-legged robots to perceive and compensate for physical interaction forces.

card.one_liner: FWBC-VLA enables contact-rich loco-manipulation using sensorless force estimation to guide VLA actions and body compensation.
card.key_idea: HSR-Force estimates interaction residuals from proprioception, which are fused into a VLA action expert via force tokens and a separate whole-body compensation generator.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on whiteboard wiping and door opening tasks using the WL&Arm dataset; outperformed baselines like OpenVLA and ForceVLA in success rates.
card.limitation: The specific impact of force estimation accuracy on overall task performance requires further investigation.

slides.title: A Wearable Pneumatic Device for Continuous, Closed-Loop, Bidirectional Tactile Interaction
slides.highlight: This system integrates tactile sensing and haptic feedback into a single pneumatic modality, improving teleoperated manipulation by reducing applied pressure and task duration.

card.one_liner: A wearable pneumatic device enabling bidirectional tactile interaction by using the same modality for sensing and feedback.
card.key_idea: A distributed architecture using proportional piezoelectric valves and local closed-loop control to regulate textile pneumatic pouches as both tactile sensors and haptic actuators.
card.evaluation: Tested via device characterization (34.2Hz bandwidth) and human studies (n=25) on force/stiffness discrimination and teleoperated pick-and-place tasks; results show improved efficiency and reduced workload.
card.limitation: Weight discrimination accuracy dropped significantly during complex teleoperation; some users conflated robotic system latency with haptic device latency.

slides.title: TacPAC: Tactile Prediction and Real-Time Action Correction in World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: TacPAC improves contact-rich manipulation by using predicted tactile observations to correct actions in real-time, significantly outperforming vision-only models.

card.one_liner: TacPAC improves contact-rich manipulation by correcting planned action chunks using real-time tactile feedback against predicted contact.
card.key_idea: A tactile expert corrects action chunks by reading current tactile images against a cached representation of the predicted contact and plan, enabling asynchronous, low-latency adjustments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-robot tasks; TacPAC averaged 64% success, outperforming T-Rex (48%) and vision-only models (22%) across 20 trials per task.

slides.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
slides.tldr: FOUNDATION MODEL FOR SUB-MILLIMETER PRECISION MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: Facet-0 utilizes a joint action-wrench proposal and a distributional Action-Wrench Critic to manage contact-rich assembly, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics-based skill acquisition and force-based interaction.

card.one_liner: Facet-0 is a robotic foundation model for sub-millimeter assembly that predicts and values contact consequences.
card.key_idea: It uses flow-matching to jointly generate action chunks and predicted wrist-wrenches, refined by a distributional Action-Wrench Critic and a lightweight bounded actor for local adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five computer-assembly tasks using ManuFacet-1K; achieved 82% mean success vs 15% for the strongest baseline with 0.5mm placement accuracy.
card.limitation: Performance drops on tasks without free-space sub-goals, such as the LEVER task, which only reached 50% success.

slides.title: Scaling Bimanual Household Manipulation from 1,500 hours of Demonstrations to On-Policy Corrections
slides.tldr: BIMANUAL MANIPULATION SCALING VIA VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a vision-language-action model trained on 1,500 hours of bimanual demonstrations and explores performance gains from real-time human intervention corrections, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: XR-2 VLA model scales bimanual household manipulation using 1,500 hours of expert and corrective data.
card.key_idea: A 5B parameter VLA model combining Qwen3-VL with a flow-matching action expert, trained on expert demonstrations and refined via failure-weighted DAgger on-policy corrections.
card.evaluation: Tested on clothes folding; expert data scaled success from 34% to 84%, while DAgger further increased it to 93% over three rounds.
card.limitation: Expert data returns diminish as the policy reaches states outside the expert distribution, requiring human-in-the-loop interventions for further gains.
